[RFC: `forbidden` and `unauthorized` · vercel/next.js · Discussion #73753 · GitHub](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/73753) 5. [How to Handle Errors in Next.js 15?](https://readmedium.com/how-to-handle-errors-in-next-js-15-7268454d976f) # Next.js 15 `forbidden()` Function Summary ## Setup To use `forbidden()` from `next/navigation`, you must enable the experimental `authInterrupts` configuration in `next.config.js`:[1] ```ts const nextConfig = { experimental: { authInterrupts: true, }, } export default nextConfig ``` ## Usage The `forbidden()` function throws an error that renders a 403 error page.[1] It can be invoked in Server Components, Server Actions, and Route Handlers to restrict access based on authorization checks:[1] ```tsx import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' export default async function AdminPage() { const session = await verifySession() if (session.role !== 'admin') { forbidden() } return

Admin Page

} ``` ## Custom Error Page Create a `forbidden.tsx` file to customize the 403 error UI:[1][4] ```tsx // app/forbidden.tsx import Link from 'next/link' export default function Forbidden() { return (

Forbidden

You are not authorized to access this resource.

Return Home
) } ``` ## Important Notes - `forbidden()` cannot be called in the root layout[1] - This feature is experimental and not recommended for production[1] - The status code will be 200 if triggered after response headers are sent[4]

events.content:
Here’s what was implemented.

### 1. **`experimental.authInterrupts`** (`next.config.ts`)

`forbidden()` from `next/navigation` only works when this flag is on, so the response can be a real **403** (verified with `curl` on a production server: `/admin` → `403`).

### 2. **`app/admin/page.tsx`**

Server Component that uses `verifyAdmin()` from your existing auth helper and calls **`forbidden()`** when `session?.role !== 'admin'`.  
`export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` keeps the check **per request** so it isn’t frozen at build time with the mock `user` role.

### 3. **`app/forbidden.tsx`**

Root-level **`forbidden.tsx`** so Next renders your custom UI for the auth “forbidden” boundary (403), with a short explanation and a link home.

With the current mock in `app/lib/auth.ts` (`role: 'user'`), `/admin` returns **403** and that page. To see the admin UI locally, temporarily set `role: 'admin'` in `getSession()`.

Reference: [Next.js `forbidden()` docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/forbidden).
